::api-operation{method="PATCH" path="/v1/businesses/{biz}/emails/ses"}
#docs
Omit `secretAccessKey` to keep the stored one; send an empty string to clear it. ⚠ This body is camelCase — `accessKeyId`, `secretAccessKey`, `configurationSet` — unlike the snake_case used elsewhere in this API. Documented as the route actually parses it (`sesSettingsSchema`) rather than normalised to look consistent, because a client following a tidied-up spec would send fields the route ignores.

## Path parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `biz` | `string` | **yes** | Business id (biz_…) |

## Headers

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Idempotency-Key` | `string` | no | Safely retry writes — repeats return the original response. If a write FAILED after it had already taken effect, that failure is what repeats: the key is spent, and a new attempt needs a new key. |

## Body

The request body is **required**.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | `boolean` | no | Whether the business sends email through its own Amazon SES account. |
| `region` | `string` | no | The AWS region used to send email. |
| `accessKeyId` | `string` | no | The AWS access key id. |
| `configurationSet` | `string` | no | The SES configuration set to attach to each send. |
| `secretAccessKey` | `string` | no | Absent keeps the stored key, '' clears it, a value replaces it. |

## Response

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `object` | `string` | The object type; always `ses_settings`. One of `ses_settings`. |
| `enabled` | `boolean` | When false, this business sends through the deployment-wide MAILER_PROVIDER. |
| `region` | `string` | The AWS region used to send email. |
| `access_key_id` | `string` | Identifies the credential; safe to render. The secret half is never returned. |
| `configuration_set` | `string` | The SES configuration set attached to each send. |
| `secret_configured` | `boolean` | Whether a secret access key is stored. Never the key itself. |
| `effective_transport` | `string` | What this business actually sends through, once SMTP/SES/platform is resolved. |
| `delivers` | `boolean` | Whether that transport can deliver — a configured transport is not necessarily a working one. |
| `effective_from_address` | `string` | The From address used for sends. |
| `effective_from_name` | `string` | The From name used for sends. |
| `from_source` | `string` | Where the From address comes from: this business or the platform. One of `business`, `platform`. |

## Status codes

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `200` | Updated |
| `400` | Invalid SES settings |
| `404` | No such business |
| `409` | Idempotency-Key conflict — the key is already in flight, or was reused with a different request payload. |

#request
```bash [Request]
curl -X PATCH "$TMBILLING_URL/v1/businesses/biz_XXXXXXXXXXXX01/emails/ses" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TMBILLING_API_KEY" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "enabled": false,
    "region": "us-east-1"
  }'
```
